headline.headline: OUTMAN BLASTS TIGERS INTO DAYLIGHT WITH SEVENTH-INNING BOMB
headline.deck: Three-run shot off Royals breaks open pitchers' duel; Dingler's eighth-inning double seals it
headline.body:
DETROIT — James Outman turned a scoreless game into a Detroit blowout with one swing, depositing a three-run homer in the seventh inning Thursday night to lift the Tigers to a 4-3 victory over the Kansas City Royals before 35,548 fans at Comerica Park. The Royals had broken the deadlock first, pushing across two runs in the sixth to take what looked like a commanding lead in a low-scoring affair. Outman's blast in the bottom of the seventh erased the deficit in a single stroke and gave Detroit a lead it would not surrender.

The Royals refused to go quietly. Kansas City scratched back for one run in the eighth inning to pull within 4-3, putting the tying run in scoring position and rattling the Detroit bullpen. But Dillon Dingler provided breathing room when his go-ahead double in the bottom of the eighth extended the margin, and the Tigers held on through a tense ninth. Dustin Anderson earned the win on the mound, improving Detroit's record in a stretch that has seen the club climb back into the AL Central conversation.

The loss dropped Kansas City, which entered the series riding a strong first half, to a precarious position in the division standings. The game took 2 hours and 46 minutes to complete. Detroit's bullpen worked out of trouble in the late innings, and the performance of Outman — acquired to provide left-handed pop in the middle of the lineup — underscored why the Tigers believed the outfielder could be a difference-maker in close games exactly like this one.

secondary.headline: TWINS OUTLAST GUARDIANS IN 12-INNING MARATHON
secondary.deck: Minnesota scores twice in the 12th to end a grueling extra-inning battle in Cleveland
secondary.body:
CLEVELAND — The Minnesota Twins scratched out two runs in the 12th inning Thursday to defeat the Cleveland Guardians 3-1 in a grinding, 3-hour-and-23-minute contest at Progressive Field. Cleveland had taken a 1-0 lead on a run in the fifth inning and nursed that slim advantage all the way to the eighth, when Minnesota finally knotted the score at one. Neither club could push across the decisive run through nine, ten, or eleven frames, setting up Minnesota's decisive two-run outburst in the 12th. Pitcher Taj Bradley earned the victory, with Morris also credited in the box score.

The Guardians left the tying run stranded in the late innings as Cleveland's offense, which managed just one run on the night, could not deliver against Minnesota's bullpen. The Twins entered the game trailing in the AL Central race and needed every one of those 12 innings to secure the road win. Attendance was 27,354.

secondary.headline: PATRICK KANE RIDES BACK INTO CHICAGO ON AN $8 MILLION PER YEAR DEAL
secondary.deck: Future Hall of Famer agrees to two-year contract with Blackhawks, ending his time away from the franchise
secondary.body:
CHICAGO — Patrick Kane is coming home. The Blackhawks and the future Hall of Fame winger have agreed to a two-year contract carrying an average annual value of $8 million, the club announced Thursday, reuniting one of the most decorated players in franchise history with the organization where he won three Stanley Cup championships. Kane, who spent time away from Chicago before this agreement, will return to a Blackhawks team in the midst of a rebuilding phase anchored by young talent developed through the draft.

The signing carries unmistakable emotional weight in a city that watched Kane win the Conn Smythe Trophy in 2013 and become the face of one of the NHL's most celebrated dynasties. Whether Kane can still contribute at a meaningful level after his absence from the Blackhawks remains the central question for Chicago's front office, but the two-year term suggests both sides see a realistic path toward postseason relevance. The deal was completed during the NHL's active free agency period, with teams across the league continuing to reshape their rosters.

secondary.headline: CELTICS LOCK UP JORDAN WALSH ON THREE-YEAR, $15 MILLION EXTENSION
secondary.deck: Boston secures the forward through the 2029-30 season as the franchise eyes another title run
secondary.body:
BOSTON — The Boston Celtics moved to secure their depth Thursday, agreeing to a three-year, $15 million contract extension with forward Jordan Walsh that will keep him in Boston through the 2029-30 season. Walsh, who has developed into a reliable rotational piece for a Celtics club that has consistently competed at the top of the Eastern Conference, gives the front office continuity as the team navigates the NBA playoffs and plans for future championship windows. The deal was confirmed by sources with knowledge of the agreement.

The extension reflects Boston's commitment to retaining players developed within its system rather than allowing them to reach the open market. Walsh figures to remain a key depth contributor on a roster built around established stars. The move comes during a busy stretch of offseason roster management across the league, with teams using summer league and early free agency activity to position themselves for the upcoming season.

column.headline: KANE'S RETURN IS A REMINDER THAT SPORTS NEVER FORGET ITS STORYBOOK ENDINGS
column.body:
There is a reason crowds in Chicago will cheer louder for Patrick Kane than for any visiting All-Star who happens to be having a better statistical season right now. Kane did not just play for the Blackhawks. He defined them across one of the most glamorous stretches any NHL franchise has assembled in the salary-cap era. Three Cups. One Conn Smythe. Countless overtime moments that burned themselves into the memory of anyone who followed the sport between 2010 and 2015. The $8 million per year figure is not a charity arrangement. It is the market acknowledging that Kane can still move the needle on the ice and in the seats.

The harder truth, of course, is that this Blackhawks team is not the Blackhawks of those championship years. Chicago is rebuilding, and Kane knows it. What makes the deal intriguing rather than merely sentimental is the two-year commitment. Both sides believe there is something to build toward, not just a farewell tour to applaud. Whether that faith proves justified will tell us something important about how much Kane has left, and about whether the Blackhawks' rebuild is further along than the standings currently suggest.

story.headline: BRAVES RALLY FROM THREE DOWN TO EDGE PADRES IN SLUGFEST
story.deck: Five home runs fly at Truist Park in Atlanta's one-run comeback win
story.body:
ATLANTA — The Atlanta Braves trailed by three runs after two innings Thursday night, then answered with a four-run fourth inning and held off a late San Diego charge to defeat the Padres 6-5 before 29,441 fans at Truist Park. The game featured five home runs and was decided by a single run in a contest that lasted just two hours and 31 minutes.

Ty France gave San Diego an early 3-1 edge with his 16th home run of the season in the second inning, but the Braves responded emphatically in the fourth. Orlando Arcia Baldwin crushed his 19th homer and Ozzie Albies connected for his 16th as Atlanta scored four times to take a 5-3 lead. A home run tagged as II No. 19 extended the advantage to 6-3 through seven innings, with Will Smith adding his seventh of the year at some point in the barrage. San Diego starter Chris Sale hit Jake Cronenworth with a pitch during the contest.

The Padres made it interesting in the eighth, scoring twice to pull within 6-5, but Atlanta closer held the line in the ninth to preserve the victory. San Diego left nine runners on base and could not overcome the deficit, leaving the Braves celebrating a one-run win that snapped a potential threat from a Padres squad that had rallied late but run out of outs.

story.headline: EDWARDS TIES THE KNOT: MINNESOTA RECORDS CONFIRM TIMBERWOLVES STAR MARRIED SHANNON JACKSON
story.deck: State marriage certificate reveals Anthony Edwards quietly wed longtime partner Shannon Jackson.
story.body:
Anthony Edwards, the electrifying Minnesota Timberwolves guard and one of the NBA's brightest young stars, is a married man. Minnesota's Official Marriage System website lists a certificate confirming Edwards wed Shannon Jackson, according to public records surfaced Friday. The 24-year-old superstar, who led Minnesota deep into the postseason and has emerged as one of the league's most marketable faces, had kept the relationship largely out of the public spotlight.

The news broke amid a busy NBA offseason that has seen plenty of roster shuffling across the league. While Edwards has made headlines for his on-court dominance, averaging over 27 points per game last season and establishing himself as a cornerstone of the Timberwolves franchise, this revelation shifts attention briefly to his personal life. Neither Edwards nor representatives from the Timberwolves organization had issued a public comment as of Friday afternoon.

The confirmation arrives as the broader NBA world churns through a frantic free agency period, with Boston locking up forward Jordan Walsh on a three-year, $15 million extension through the 2029-30 season, and speculation swirling around LeBron James and a reported Miami Heat social media post that analyst Stephen A. Smith publicly dismissed as insignificant. For Edwards, whether on the court or off it, the spotlight never seems to dim.

story.headline: KANE COMES HOME: BLACKHAWKS REUNITE WITH FUTURE HALL OF FAMER ON TWO-YEAR DEAL
story.deck: Chicago brings back its franchise icon at $8 million per year to mentor a rising young core.
story.body:
CHICAGO -- Patrick Kane is a Blackhawk again. The 37-year-old winger, whose surgically repaired hip had kept him off the ice for stretches of recent seasons, agreed to a two-year contract with Chicago on Friday carrying an average annual value of $8 million, reuniting him with the franchise where he won three Stanley Cup championships alongside Jonathan Toews and became one of the most electrifying players of his generation.

The move carries unmistakable symbolism for an organization that has spent the past three seasons dismantling its dynasty and rebuilding around generational center Connor Bedard. General manager Kyle Davidson is betting that Kane's playoff pedigree, his dazzling playmaking instincts and his sheer star power can accelerate Bedard's development while selling tickets at the United Center to a fan base that has endured significant growing pains. Kane, a Buffalo native who was drafted first overall by Chicago in 2007, spent 15 seasons with the Blackhawks before departing for the New York Rangers in 2023.

The signing lands on the same day Columbus locked up goaltender Jet Greaves on a three-year, $15 million deal, and as Dallas GM Jim Nill reiterated his intention to sign restricted free agent winger Jason Robertson to a long-term contract. But no transaction on this July Friday carried the weight of Kane pulling on the Indian head sweater one more time, giving Chicago and its rebuilding nucleus something it has sorely lacked since the championship window slammed shut: a living, breathing connection to what winning looks like.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026
story.deck: Several franchises are reshaping their rosters around new signal-callers this spring.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a full-blown quarterback market, with teams across the league scrambling to secure their franchise player heading into the 2026 season. The Las Vegas Raiders made the most aggressive move of the spring, agreeing to a four-year, $192 million contract with free agent quarterback Sam Darnold, banking on the veteran's late-career resurgence to anchor a retooled offense under new head coach Mike Vrabel, who departed New England to take the Las Vegas job in March.

The Cleveland Browns, desperate to escape years of instability at the position, sent a package of three draft picks to the Carolina Panthers in exchange for Bryce Young, reuniting the young quarterback with offensive coordinator Tommy Rees, who called plays in Charlotte last season. Browns general manager Andrew Berry called the deal a calculated risk, noting that Young's mobility and arm talent remain elite despite his rocky tenure in Carolina. The Panthers, flush with picks, are widely expected to target a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 draft.

Meanwhile, the 2026 NFL Draft last month produced its own share of controversy after Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders slipped to the third round amid questions about his arm strength at the combine. The Pittsburgh Steelers nabbed him at pick 78 and immediately drew praise from analysts who believe his football IQ and pocket presence fit coordinator Arthur Smith's system perfectly. NFL Network draft analyst Daniel Jeremiah called the selection the steal of the entire draft class, a sentiment echoed loudly across social media within hours of the pick.
